ALMOST KILLED MY CAT!

I would absolutely NOT recommend this clinic after what happened to my cat.

I originally brought my cat in for urinary problems and was told he had a simple UTI. he had gotten placed a catheter here. After he accidentally pulled it out, we had to bring him back to have it replaced.

One day before his scheduled removal, the catheter became blocked. We immediately brought him back because we knew something was wrong. They removed the catheter, sent him home, and insisted he was fine.

He was NOT fine.

A few hours later, my cat struggled to urinate, vomited, began breathing heavily, and became extremely unwell. He looked like he was dying. We had to rush him to an emergency vet, where they confirmed that he was critically ill and told us he was dying. We were told that if we had waited even a few hours, he likely would not have made it.

The emergency vet also raised serious concerns about how his catheter had been managed. We were told that, in their professional opinion, the catheter should not have been left in for that length of time and that his urine should have been collected and monitored for examination rather than simply being allowed to drip out.

Ultimately, my cat needed PU surgery because of his urinary problems, which permanently changed his anatomy.

Throughout our experience with this clinic, they seemed unsure about their own work and couldn’t give us a definite answer about whether our cat was actually okay. We were also later blamed for “not following proper aftercare,” despite doing everything we could and repeatedly bringing him back when we knew something was wrong.

They also later claimed that we had refused or tried to deny our cat fluids. That is NOT what happened. We were discussing how we were going to pay for the fluids while they insisted they would give them to him. We never intended to deny him necessary treatment, so portraying this as though they made some huge sacrifice for us was extremely upsetting.

Honestly, throughout this experience, it felt like the clinic cared more about money and protecting themselves than putting our pet first.

I trusted this clinic with my cat’s LIFE, and we were told he was “fine” only for him to become critically ill hours later. This was not a minor inconvenience — this was our beloved pet’s life. Knowing that he could have died because we were told he was fine is something I will never get over.

We have also made a formal complaint regarding the care our cat received because we believe this situation needs to be properly reviewed.

I am beyond angry and disappointed. We will NEVER be taking our cats back here, and I strongly recommend that other pet owners think twice before going into this clinic with their beloved pets.

Lie: I was specifically told I needed to bring my male cat back after his neuter to have his “internal stitches” removed. After questioning this, I confirmed with a reputable veterinarian that this made absolutely no sense. Internal sutures are not something an owner is normally told to return to have removed after a routine neuter.

Cheat: That supposed “stitch removal” got me back through their doors. Once I arrived, I was then told they couldn’t take my cat to the back without additional services, including a full blood panel and more vaccinations, even though he had recently been vaccinated and wasn’t due for his boosters for another two weeks. I independently confirmed the vaccine timing with another reputable veterinarian.

Steal: And it wasn’t just my experience. Every time I sat in that waiting room, I watched people who clearly loved their animals being presented with more charges, more tests, and more things they were told their pets “needed.” It was incredibly disturbing to watch.

Pet owners are vulnerable when something involves the health and safety of an animal they love. We rely on veterinary professionals to give us honest medical guidance, not to use our concern for our pets as an opportunity to keep adding charges.

I have no problem paying for necessary veterinary care. What I have a serious problem with is being given questionable or misleading information that gets me through the door, only to be told I need to spend even more money once I’m there.

Based on my experience, I do not trust this clinic, its recommendations, or its business practices. I strongly encourage anyone considering bringing their pet here to ask questions, request an itemized explanation of every recommended service, and get a second veterinary opinion before agreeing to additional procedures, testing, or vaccinations.

People trying to do the right thing for their animals deserve honesty, not a sales pitch disguised as medical necessity.

I was also concerned to find several inaccuracies in Bandit's medical records, including information stating that he had been experiencing vomiting and diarrhea for 5–7 days, which I did not report during the visit. I have requested clarification regarding these discrepancies.

Additionally, Bandit developed significant bruising at the blood draw site following his visit.

I contacted the clinic directly regarding these concerns and waited several days for a response. As a pet owner, I expect accurate medical records, careful prescribing practices, and timely communication when serious concerns are raised. Based on my experience, I would encourage other pet owners to ask questions, review all prescriptions carefully, and seek a second opinion if something does not seem right.

We found this place through the ACS website. We fully understand that Petshotz is not an actual ACS clinic, but they are listed as a partner/affiliated clinic. When we called to make an appointment to have our dog spayed, we clearly told them multiple times that we live in a qualifying zip code for the free spay program through ACS. Over the 3–4 days leading up to the appointment, we spoke with staff several times and I confirmed repeatedly that the spay itself would be free and that we would only be paying roughly $100 for vaccines and a microchip.
When we arrived for the appointment, we were suddenly told the total was $282, and the receptionist insisted we were NEVER quoted $100 and that I was mistaken. Not only was this incredibly frustrating, but the receptionist was extremely rude and dismissive. We nearly walked out, but our dog had already been fasting for almost 10 hours and does not tolerate car rides well, so we felt pressured to continue because her health and comfort came first. We decided we would just figure out how to cover the unexpected cost later.
We dropped her off around 9:30 AM. At 12:30 PM we received a call saying that once they opened her up, she was in heat and the procedure would cost extra. Fine. we weren’t happy, but we weren’t going to have them close her back up mid-surgery.
Then we were told she was dehydrated and needed fluids at an additional charge. Of course she was dehydrated her appointment was scheduled for 9 AM and by that point she had gone more than 12 hours without food or water as instructed. Again, we paid because they literally had our dog and we had no real choice.
When we picked her up, we asked to speak to a manager because the pricing kept changing and the receptionist’s behavior was unacceptable. The manager claimed the higher cost was because we supposedly agreed to additional blood tests costing $90 when checking in. We were asked about X-rays, which we declined, but we were NEVER asked about blood work. The manager stated she spoke with staff and insisted we had been asked. We were not.
At discharge we were told to return in 7 days for stitch removal. I specifically confirmed that this follow-up was included in what we had already paid, and I was told yes, unless there was an infection.
Seven days later we returned. Immediately we were told her incision looked inflamed because of the surgery suit we used to prevent our other dog from licking the area. They charged us another $25 just to evaluate the incision before removing stitches. Nearly an hour later, we were told it was “infected” and that we would now need to pay $205 more for stitch removal and medication.
We keep our dog clean and monitored closely. I am not a veterinarian, but I struggle to understand how a soft surgery suit is supposedly worse than a dog laying directly on her abdomen — something dogs naturally do all day.
At that point, we refused further treatment there and sought a second opinion elsewhere. The second veterinarian confirmed there was no infection. We were also told this was not the first time they had seen pets come from this clinic after experiencing questionable billing practices.
Between the constant price changes, charges for services we did not consent to, being told we were “wrong” about quotes we confirmed multiple times, and the rude treatment from staff, this entire experience felt dishonest and predatory.
We came here trusting an ACS partner clinic to provide affordable care. Instead, we left feeling misled, financially pressured, and deeply disappointed.

Editing just so everyone is aware:
I am filing a complaint with the better business bureau, and ACS. In case you don’t feel like that is a big enough deal, ACS is run off of federal and state grants and MONITORED by those organizations so any complaints listed are investigated thoroughly and we were told by ACS it isn’t the first complaint and the chances of being removed off of the ACS partner list is high.

*Disappointing Experience at Pet Shots*

I've tried to give Pet Shots the benefit of the doubt, but my experiences have been consistently frustrating. My first few visits were fine, despite long wait times, which I attributed to the clinic's small size and busy schedule.

However, my last two visits were disappointing. Despite having an appointment, I was still made to wait while walk-ins were prioritized. The excuse given was that they needed to administer vaccines, but this raises questions about the point of making appointments.

I ended up taking my cat to another vet for a consultation, which was a much better experience. When I returned to Pet Shots for my cat's neutering, I was quoted $63, (zipcode eligibility) microchip is required & one extra shot he still needed,which seemed reasonable.

However, things took a turn when they tried to charge me extra for a check-up, claiming that my cat needed additional blood work. Vet tech told me to call the clinic & they quickly  provided proof of my cat's recent lab work from another clinic, which showed that everything was within normal limits. Dr from clinic said my cat was good to go to get fixed. I even offered for the Vet tech to talk to the Dr while I was on the phone so we could proceed onto the next, and he denied too.

I was frustrated by the runaround and the insistence on additional charges. As a customer, it's disappointing to feel like you're being nickel-and-dimed.

I understand what’s recommended and all I ever want is my fur babies to be taken care off,  but if I feel like it’s always inconsistent is where I begin to question.
And adding more blood work on top of surgery would have been to much trauma on the body for my kitten. But that’s just my own opinion.

I found another clinic that was happy to help, and they didn't have any issues with the info I provided & concerns.

I really tried to give the benefit of the doubt by going back but not anymore.

*Advice to Others*

Be cautious of extra charges, and make sure to ask all the necessary questions before leaving and paying. While I don't doubt that Pet Shots cares for animals, I would not recommend this clinic due to their business practices.
